summary: Autoscaler learning drift on model-variant rollout triggered short-lived GPU deficit in dedicated pool
description:
Issue summary: After a staged rollout of a new variant (rwkv-alpha-7b-quantized-8bit) for BrightCart's reserved pool, we observed a 3-6 minute window of GPU shortage in the customer's dedicated pool causing p99 latency spikes and 429-level throttles for a subset of their routes. Impact included request fallbacks to lower-capacity model variants and transient user-facing errors.

Impact: BrightCart reported increased error rate and user latency during peak morning window (~09:30-09:36 UTC). Estimated affected requests ~1.2k, p99 generation latency increased from 220ms to ~1.8s for affected tenants. No data leakage or security events observed.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Roll forward model variant to rwkv-alpha-7b-quantized-8bit in a reserved pool with moderate burst traffic patterns
2) Generate a mix of short (~30 tokens) and medium (~250 tokens) chat completions from multiple client shards to emulate BrightCart's load profile
3) Observe autoscaler predicted GPU need vs actual attach rate in the autoscaler dashboard; check dedicated pool attach failures and fallback events
4) Revert variant to previous model and repeat to verify mitigation
logs: 2026-03-14T09:32:12Z scheduler: allocated_temp_capacity=+4 gpus for reserved pool brightcart-resv-12
investigation_notes: Initial triage: metrics show mismatch between autoscaler prediction signal (based on historical request shapes) and actual instantaneous demand following the variant rollout.

Serving runtime reported a modest increase in per-request KV cache usage for the quantized variant; cold-start attach times increased by ~120ms on average, compounding attach churn during a short burst window.

Autoscaler model uses features aggregated over 5-minute windows and assumes stable latency distribution; recent rollout changed distribution (more mid-length requests and larger KV fingerprints), causing underprediction for short bursts.
No underlying GPU hardware failures found; evictions and preemptions did not spike in cloud provider logs during the event.
hypothesis: Primary: Autoscaler's learned predictor experienced concept drift because the model-variant changed request size and KV cache behavior; the predictor under-allocated for a burst pattern that occurred during rollout.

Secondary: Serving-runtime attach latency increase (due to larger KV handling in the new variant) amplified the perceived shortage by delaying slot availability while autoscaler was still reacting on aggregated signals.
Tertiary: A small noisy tenant in the same reserved pool increased short-lived ephemeral connections at the exact same window, pushing attach contention over the threshold.
findings: Confirmed autoscaler underpredicted needed GPUs by ~30% for the 3-minute window (predicted 12 vs observed peak attach demand 17).
KV cache footprint per session increased ~18% for the new quantized variant compared to previous baseline, increasing attach time by ~120ms median.
A background tenant (non-critical) had a transient burst that contributed ~8% of extra attaches during the window.
root_cause: Concept drift in autoscaler's demand predictor caused by rollout of a model variant with different request-length and KV cache characteristics; serving-runtime attach latency increase amplified attach contention and led to a short-lived GPU deficit in the dedicated pool.
resolution: Immediate mitigation applied (09:33 UTC): temporary +4 GPU emergency capacity injected into BrightCart's reserved pool; rollout paused and variant pinned back to previous model for critical routes.
Autoscaler fallback thresholds adjusted to be more aggressive for dedicated pools handling bursty traffic (change rolled at 10:05 UTC).
Routing: added a short-term routing policy to prefer low-latency model variant for checkout and payment routes while autoscaler retraining is scheduled.
Customer update provided: BrightCart notified that we paused their variant rollout, injected capacity, and will follow up with a post-incident plan.
follow_up_actions: 1) Retrain autoscaler predictor including features for model-variant metadata (expected to remove blindspot); owner: infra-ml team; ETA 2026-03-20
2) Add rollout-aware guardrail: during staged rollouts, autoscaler enters conservative mode and temporarily raises headroom for dedicated pools; owner: autoscaler team; ETA 2026-03-18
3) Instrument serving-runtime to emit per-variant KV cache footprint metric (done as PR #1901); owner: serving-runtime; ETA 2026-03-16
4) Postmortem write-up and customer-facing summary; owner: support/solutions; ETA 2026-03-17
5) Evaluate noisy-tenant isolation knobs for reserved pools and add detection alarms; owner: scheduler team; ETA 2026-04-01
